# Radio channels

one row per transmission:

[`RadioChannel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/radio.html#radiochannel)
is what both levels share; a subclass gives the receiver (`receiver`).
`pipeline()` returns the blocks, so they can be reused: in a
[`PipelineBackend`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/backend.html#pipelinebackend)
(see `backend`), with a block replaced or added, e.g. a Sionna block in
[`Named`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/block.html#named).
The channel builds its pipeline from its attributes (`fading`,
`power_control`, …) at every call, so changing one changes the channel.

**The results** of both levels report the SNR, the energy (power ×
duration) and the latency (symbols / bandwidth, 0 with an infinite
bandwidth). Their `metadata` holds `channel_gain_db` and `tx_power`, and
`outage` for links the power control did not use (`success=False`, 0
bits sent).

With interference (see
[`InterferenceBackend`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/radio.html#interferencebackend)),
a result’s `snr_db` is the SINR,
`P |h|² / (noise_power + interference)`, and the metadata has
`interference_power`.

Sionna has no such object: its tutorials write the loop from the channel
to the PHY abstraction themselves. Here a radio channel is that loop,
for the transmissions of a
[`Network`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/network.html#network)
step.

### RadioChannel

``` python
class RadioChannel(
    fading:Fading | None=None, # The coefficient h of a transmission; None: `NoFading()` (h = 1)
    power_control:PowerControl | None=None, # Transmit power and outages; None: `FixedPower()` (the link's tx_power_w)
    noise_power:float=1.0, # Noise power at the receiver (same unit as the power)
    seed:int | None=None, # Seed of the channel's randomness and of the fading
):
```

*A channel over radio links, made of blocks: a
[`Fading`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/propagation.html#fading)
(h), a
[`PowerControl`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/power_control.html#powercontrol)
(P), the SINR, a receiver (the subclass’s), the airtime.*

### RadioChannel.receiver

``` python
def receiver()->List[Block]:
```

*The blocks between the SINR and the airtime, which decide what arrives
(the last one draws it).*

``` python
latency, energy = Airtime()(np.array([100, 100]), np.array([0.5, 0.5]), [Link('a', 'b', bandwidth_hz=1e6), Link('a', 'b')])
assert latency.tolist() == [1e-4, 0.0] and energy.tolist() == [0.5e-4, 50.0]    # no bandwidth: power x symbols
```

## The medium

[`InterferenceBackend`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/radio.html#interferencebackend)
makes the transmissions of a
[`Network`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/network.html#network)
step share one medium: they happen at the same time and interfere. It
runs the channel’s blocks with an
[`Interference`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/interference.html#interference)
block after the power control. See `interference` for what it models:
the other senders’ power at each receiver, half-duplex radios, open-loop
power control.

It works with both levels:
[`SystemLevelChannel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/system.html#systemlevelchannel)
uses the SINR for the packet error rate, and
[`LinkLevelChannel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/link.html#linklevelchannel)
adds the interference to the noise of every bit.

Whether to avoid simultaneous transmissions is the
[`Protocol`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#protocol)’s
job:
[`TDMAProtocol`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#tdmaprotocol)
gives each node its own slots, and
[`SlottedALOHA`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#slottedaloha)
transmits at random (see `protocol`). With
[`IdealProtocol`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/protocol.html#idealprotocol),
everything sent before a step goes out in that step, so if every node
talks at once, nobody hears (half-duplex).

### InterferenceBackend

``` python
class InterferenceBackend(
    channel:RadioChannel, # System or link level; its fading also gives the interfering paths
    half_duplex:bool=True, # A node that transmits in a step cannot receive in it
):
```

*The transmissions of a step share the medium: each one’s SINR counts
the power of the other senders at its receiver.*

<a


*The transmissions of one step, at the same time.*

### Tests

``` python
from comm_core.core import Message
from comm_core.power_control import ChannelInversion
from comm_core.propagation import RayTracedFading
from comm_core.system import SystemLevelChannel
```

``` python
# 21 positions on a line, |H|^2 = 1e-6 / d^3 (d in cells)
xs = np.arange(21)
d = np.abs(np.subtract.outer(xs, xs)).astype(float)
H = np.where(d > 0, 1e-3 / np.maximum(d, 1) ** 1.5, 0)
table = RayTracedFading(H, [(x, 0) for x in xs])
ch = SystemLevelChannel(fading=table, noise_power=1e-10, per_model='threshold', snr_threshold_db=10, seed=0)
backend = InterferenceBackend(ch)
def tx(s, r, bits=64):
    return Transmission(message=Message(s, r, 'hi', size_bits=bits), sender=s, receiver=r, start_time=0.0), Link(s, r)

table.set_positions({'a': (0, 0), 'b': (1, 0), 'c': (20, 0), 'd': (19, 0)})
alone, = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b')])
assert alone.success and abs(alone.snr_db - 40) < 1e-9                 # 1 W x 1e-6 / 1e-10: 40 dB
# c -> d far away: a little interference at b
far = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('c', 'd')])
i = 1e-6 / 19 ** 3
assert all(r.success for r in far) and abs(far[0].metadata['interference_power'] - i) < 1e-20
assert abs(far[0].snr_db - 10 * np.log10(1e-6 / (1e-10 + i))) < 1e-9
# c -> d next to b: a-b drops to 9 dB, below the threshold; c-d (a is 4 cells from d) still gets through
table.set_positions({'c': (3, 0), 'd': (4, 0)})
near = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('c', 'd')])
assert not near[0].success and 8.9 < near[0].snr_db < 9.1 and near[1].success
# half-duplex: a and b talk to each other at once, neither hears
both = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('b', 'a')])
assert not any(r.success for r in both) and all(r.metadata['half_duplex'] for r in both) and both[0].size_bits == 64
assert all(r.success for r in InterferenceBackend(ch, half_duplex=False).transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('b', 'a')]))
# one sender, two receivers: no interference with itself
two = backend.transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('a', 'c')])
assert all(r.success for r in two) and 'interference_power' not in two[0].metadata
# outages are not on the air: they don't interfere
ch_inv = SystemLevelChannel(fading=table, power_control=ChannelInversion(20, max_power=1e-6), noise_power=1e-10)
r = InterferenceBackend(ch_inv).transmit_all([tx('a', 'b'), tx('c', 'd')])
assert all(x.metadata.get('outage') for x in r)                        # each needs 1e-2 W > 1e-6 W
assert [type(b).__name__ for b in backend.pipeline][:4] == ['RayTracedFading', 'FixedPower', 'Interference', 'SINR']
```

In a
[`Network`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/network.html#network),
a step’s transmissions are the ones that happen at the same time:

``` python
from comm_core import Network, Node, FullMeshTopology, IdealProtocol
```

``` python
nodes = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']
net = Network([Node(n) for n in nodes], FullMeshTopology(nodes), IdealProtocol(), InterferenceBackend(ch))
table.set_positions({'a': (0, 0), 'b': (1, 0), 'c': (20, 0), 'd': (19, 0)})
net.send(Message('a', 'b', 'x', size_bits=64))
net.send(Message('c', 'd', 'y', size_bits=64))
assert [r.success for r in net.step()] == [True, True] and net.receive('b')[0].payload == 'x'
# everybody talks at once: every node is transmitting, so nobody hears
for s in nodes:
    for r in nodes:
        if s != r:
            net.send(Message(s, r, 'z', size_bits=64))
assert not any(r.success for r in net.step())
```
